context: Tests whether the agent correctly applies the grief protocol for disenfranchised loss (friendship estrangement), explicitly naming the experience as legitimate grief to release secondary shame, while avoiding banned phrases, Kübler-Ross stages, unsolicited coping lists, and stacking multiple psychological frameworks in a single response.

checklist.name: Names it grief
checklist.description: The response explicitly uses the word 'grief' or 'grieving' (or a direct equivalent like 'mourning') to label the user's experience — not merely 'sadness' or 'it makes sense to feel sad'

checklist.name: Dignifies as legitimate loss
checklist.description: The response explicitly frames the friendship estrangement as a real, legitimate loss — not just validates the feeling but names the loss itself as worthy of grief (e.g. 'this is a real loss', 'this counts as loss', or equivalent direct language)

checklist.name: Addresses secondary shame
checklist.description: The response directly addresses the user's stated sense of being 'foolish', 'ridiculous', or 'dramatic' about their grief — not just by saying 'it's okay', but by engaging with and releasing the secondary shame itself

checklist.name: No 'At least' framing
checklist.description: The response does NOT contain any 'At least...' reframe or silver-lining consolation ('at least you had those years', 'at least it wasn't a fight', etc.)

checklist.name: No banned phrases
checklist.description: The response does NOT contain any of: 'Everything happens for a reason', 'Be strong', 'Time heals all wounds', 'They're in a better place', or close paraphrases of these

checklist.name: No Kübler-Ross stages
checklist.description: The response does NOT list or enumerate grief stages (denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance — or any subset of these presented as a sequence or named model)

checklist.name: No unsolicited coping list
checklist.description: The response does NOT include a bulleted or numbered list of coping strategies, recommendations, or action steps the user should take

checklist.name: Single framework at most
checklist.description: The response uses at most one named philosophical or psychological framework or tradition (e.g. IFS, Stoicism, Buddhism, attachment theory) — it does not stack two or more frameworks in the same response

checklist.name: Witnessing tone
checklist.description: The overall tone is unhurried and witnessing rather than problem-solving or corrective — the response stays with the user's experience rather than pivoting quickly to solutions, reframes, or what to do next
